chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from al-Husayn ibn Hashim and Muhammad ibn Ziyad, all of them, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), like it.

Except that he said: 'If he is certain that what he left is sufficient to cover all his debt, then he should not spend from it for them (the heirs); and if he is not certain, then he should spend from the middle of the wealth for them.'

key_terms.وَسَطِ الْمَالِ: the middle of the wealth / a portion of the wealth

ai.seo_question: How should an heir handle uncertain debts when distributing an estate according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib al-ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) versus *ihtiyat* (precaution) in debt settlement. It establishes that certainty (*yaqin*) of sufficiency allows for immediate distribution, while mere uncertainty (*shakk*) mandates reserving a middle portion (*min wasat al-mal*) to ensure creditors are not shortchanged, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on protecting financial rights.
